project: dml-autoseed: rescue vacuous DELETE/UPDATE questions by seeding the missing row inside the savepoint

arch_decisions.req: Derive a one-row INSERT from a DML model answer's WHERE clause, refusing anything outside a deliberately narrow grammar. This is the shared module every other decision depends on; it is a NEW file with no dependencies of its own.
arch_decisions.decision:
Create NEW file backend/internal/repository/dml_autoseed.go (package repository) plus its unit test backend/internal/repository/dml_autoseed_test.go. No SQL parser is vendored and pg_query_go would add a cgo/C dependency, so hand-roll a narrow recogniser: anything it does not fully understand is REFUSED, and refusal is a designed outcome (ARCH-039 turns it into a lecturer-facing message). PUBLIC/PACKAGE API — every other TODO codes against exactly these signatures, do not rename them:

  type AutoSeedColumn struct { Name string `json:"name"`; Value string `json:"value"` }
  type AutoSeedPlan struct { Table string `json:"table"`; Columns []AutoSeedColumn `json:"columns"` }
  type TableColumn struct { Name string; IsNullable bool; HasDefault bool }
  var ErrAutoSeedUnsupported = errors.New(...)   // sentinel wrapped by every refusal
  func deriveAutoSeed(correctSQL, targetTable string, cols []TableColumn) (*AutoSeedPlan, error)
  func fetchTableColumns(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, schema, table string) ([]TableColumn, error)
  func applyAutoSeed(ctx context.Context, tx pgx.Tx, plan *AutoSeedPlan) error   // nil/empty plan => no-op, returns nil
  func marshalAutoSeed(plan *AutoSeedPlan) ([]byte, error)                       // nil plan => nil, nil
  func unmarshalAutoSeed(raw []byte) (*AutoSeedPlan, error)                      // len 0 or JSON null => nil, nil

ACCEPTED GRAMMAR (case-insensitive keywords, optional trailing semicolon, comments stripped):
  DELETE FROM <table> WHERE <col> = <literal> [ AND <col> = <literal> ]*
  UPDATE <table> SET <anything> WHERE <col> = <literal> [ AND <col> = <literal> ]*
<literal> is a single-quoted string with '' escape honoured, a numeric literal, or TRUE/FALSE. REFUSE (with a reason naming the offending construct): any operator other than =, OR, NOT, parentheses anywhere in the predicate, IN, LIKE/ILIKE, BETWEEN, IS NULL / IS NOT NULL, subqueries, USING/FROM joins, function calls, column-to-column comparison, more than one statement, and INSERT questions entirely (an INSERT that affects 0 rows is an INSERT ... SELECT over an empty source, which seeding cannot fix). For UPDATE, the SET list is skipped over WITHOUT being parsed — only the tail after the top-level WHERE is analysed — but a SET clause containing a parenthesised subquery or a semicolon must still cause a refusal rather than a mis-split.

COLUMN RECONCILIATION against the cols slice (which fetchTableColumns loads from information_schema.columns, treating identity/generated columns as HasDefault=true): a column pinned by an = in the WHERE is included in the plan; an unpinned column that is nullable or has a default is omitted; an unpinned NOT NULL column with no default is a REFUSAL naming the column; a pinned name that is not a column of the table is a REFUSAL naming it. Column-name matching is case-insensitive on the unquoted form, and double-quoted identifiers in the WHERE are matched case-sensitively on their unquoted content.

VALUE ENCODING: AutoSeedColumn.Value is ALWAYS a string, never a JSON number or boolean, and applyAutoSeed binds it as a text parameter so Postgres coerces it to the column's type. This is load-bearing: a JSON number round-trips through float64 and silently corrupts large integers and NUMERIC values. String literals are stored with the surrounding quotes removed and '' unescaped to a single quote.

applyAutoSeed builds INSERT INTO <pgx.Identifier{plan.Table}.Sanitize()> (<sanitized cols>) VALUES ($1,...,$N) and executes it with the values as BIND PARAMETERS — literals are never string-interpolated into SQL, so the seed carries no injection surface. Table and column identifiers go through pgx.Identifier{...}.Sanitize(); the plan is schema-unqualified and relies on the caller's search_path.

ERROR TEXT: every refusal returns an error wrapping ErrAutoSeedUnsupported whose Error() is the REASON CLAUSE ONLY, lowercase, no trailing period — e.g. `the WHERE clause uses '>' on "salary", which does not pin a single value` or `column "hire_date" is NOT NULL with no default and your WHERE clause does not pin a value for it`. ARCH-039's callers add the prefix and the trailing advice sentence. Do NOT embed the prefix here.
arch_decisions.rationale: The agreed fallback is 'refuse with a specific reason', which is exactly what makes a narrow hand-rolled recogniser sufficient — it never has to be right about SQL it does not recognise, only honest about not recognising it. Isolating everything in one new file with a frozen signature list lets the capture, evaluation, model and frontend TODOs run in parallel against a declared contract. Text-bound parameters remove both the injection surface and the float64 precision hazard.
acceptance: deriveAutoSeed("DELETE FROM employee WHERE ssn = '999999999'", "employee", cols) returns a plan with Table=employee and one column {ssn, 999999999} when every other column is nullable or defaulted.
Multi-predicate AND is supported: WHERE ssn='1' AND dno=5 yields two columns, values "1" and "5", both as Go strings.
UPDATE ... SET salary=1 WHERE ssn='9' derives from the WHERE only; the SET list is never treated as a predicate.
Each of these refuses with ErrAutoSeedUnsupported and a reason naming the construct: '>' comparison, OR, IN (...), a subquery, BETWEEN, IS NULL, two statements separated by ';', an INSERT statement.
An unpinned NOT NULL no-default column refuses with a message containing that column's name; a WHERE pinning a column absent from cols refuses naming that column.
AutoSeedColumn.Value is a string for numeric and boolean literals too; marshalAutoSeed output contains "value":"5" not "value":5.
applyAutoSeed(ctx, tx, nil) returns nil without executing anything.
applyAutoSeed passes values as bind parameters — the generated SQL text contains $1..$N and none of the literal values.
go build ./... and go vet ./... pass; dml_autoseed_test.go runs with no database and covers every refusal class listed above.

arch_decisions.req: Persist the derived plan: add the auto_seed JSONB column to both question tables, for fresh installs and for upgrades.
arch_decisions.decision: In backend/internal/repository/postgres_schema.go InitializeSystemTables, add `auto_seed JSONB` (nullable, no default) to the CREATE TABLE bodies of app.questions (near expected_rows_affected at :865) and app.practice_questions (near :916), AND append two idempotent entries to the extraMigrations slice immediately alongside the existing expected_rows_affected pair at :1086-1087: "ALTER TABLE app.questions ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS auto_seed JSONB" and "ALTER TABLE app.practice_questions ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS auto_seed JSONB". No backfill, no constraint, no index. This is the ONLY edit to postgres_schema.go for this feature — do not touch grants, roles or any other statement in the file.
arch_decisions.rationale: Mirrors the established expected_rows_affected pattern exactly (columns in both the CREATE TABLE body and extraMigrations) so fresh installs and upgraded databases converge, and the migration is re-runnable at every boot. Keeping this decision to a column-only edit is what lets it run in parallel with the derivation module and the model changes.
acceptance: Fresh DB: information_schema.columns shows app.questions.auto_seed and app.practice_questions.auto_seed, both jsonb and nullable.
Upgrade DB with the column absent: a boot adds it; a second boot re-runs without error.
Pre-existing rows read back auto_seed = NULL.
go build ./... succeeds and no behaviour other than the added column changes.

arch_decisions.req: Show the lecturer the row the system invented on their behalf, read-only.
arch_decisions.decision: In frontend/src/components/PracticeAuthoring.vue add a read-only 'Auto-seeded row' panel directly beneath the existing Correct SQL field (the block at ~:647-657), rendered only when the loaded question has a non-null auto_seed. It renders the plan as a human-readable INSERT — `INSERT INTO <table> (<cols>) VALUES (<values>)` — with a one-line explanation: this row does not exist in the category database; the system adds it inside a transaction that is rolled back, so the real database is unchanged. It is display-only: no v-model, no form field, never sent in a create/update request body. Add the matching `auto_seed?: string | null` (or a typed AutoSeedPlan interface) to the practice question type in frontend/src/services/practice.ts. Apply the same panel to the exam authoring form if and only if it lives in a file this TODO already owns; otherwise report it as out of scope rather than reaching outside file_scope. Follow the surrounding field/label/muted-text conventions already used in the form; do not restyle neighbouring fields.
arch_decisions.rationale: The approved approach has the system derive the row rather than the lecturer writing it, but data invented on someone's behalf must be visible rather than silent — otherwise a lecturer cannot tell why their question suddenly saves, or audit what students will see. Read-only keeps the single source of truth in the backend derivation.
acceptance: Editing a question whose auto_seed is non-null shows the panel with the rendered INSERT; a question with auto_seed null or absent shows nothing at all (no empty box, no placeholder).
The panel is not an input: no v-model binding, and the create/update request body is byte-identical to before this change.
npm run build (or the project's typecheck script) passes in frontend/.
No existing field's markup, layout or styling changes.

arch_decisions.req: Rescue the 0-row capture at BOTH capture sites, and replace the one-size error with reasons that say why auto-seed could not help.
arch_decisions.decision:
Depends on ARCH-038 (derivation API) and ARCH-040a/b (column + model field). Two sites, identical treatment:
  (1) backend/internal/repository/postgres_practice.go captureExpectedResult (:424-470), 0-row branch at :445
  (2) backend/internal/repository/postgres_questions.go, 0-row branch at :117
Today each sets status=failed with one fixed string. Replace that branch with: take a NESTED savepoint (SAVEPOINT autoseed) inside the existing capture transaction; call fetchTableColumns for the question's target_table in the capture schema; call deriveAutoSeed(q.CorrectSQL, q.TargetTable, cols). On refusal (errors.Is ErrAutoSeedUnsupported) set status=failed and captureErr = "Model answer affected 0 rows. Auto-seed could not build a matching row: " + err.Error() + ". Use = comparisons on the columns you want seeded, or fix the seed data in this category's database." and return errCaptureFailed as today. On success call applyAutoSeed; if the INSERT itself errors, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT autoseed first (the transaction is aborted, so every other statement would fail — this mirrors the ARCH-021 ordering rule) then set captureErr = "Model answer affected 0 rows. Auto-seed built a row but inserting it failed: " + <pg error> + "." and fail. On a successful seed, RE-RUN q.CorrectSQL: if it still affects 0 rows, fail with "Model answer affected 0 rows, and still affected 0 rows after auto-seeding a matching row. Check the WHERE clause of the correct SQL."; otherwise proceed exactly as the existing success path does — set expectedRowsAffected from the re-run tag and capture the post-image with the existing SELECT * FROM <target> — and persist the plan via marshalAutoSeed into the new auto_seed column. INSERT-type questions skip derivation entirely and keep today's message. Also thread auto_seed through the persistence and read statements this decision's two files own: the insert/upsert in postgres_questions.go (:171-211) and the insert/update/read statements in postgres_practice.go (:408-415, :589-597, :608-654), plus the read column lists at postgres_questions.go :355-369 and :387-408. Questions that capture successfully on the FIRST run must never invoke derivation and must persist auto_seed as NULL. Do not edit postgres_evaluation.go, postgres_schema.go or any models file — other TODOs own those.
arch_decisions.rationale: Auto-seed is a rescue, not a default: keeping derivation strictly on the previously-fatal 0-row branch means every question that works today takes a byte-identical path and the blast radius is a branch that could only produce an error before. Persisting the derived plan rather than re-deriving at grade time guarantees grading replays exactly what capture validated. The nested savepoint keeps a failed seed from poisoning the capture transaction, and rolling back before touching anything else follows the ARCH-021 rule already proven on the evaluation paths.
acceptance: A DELETE against a row that does not exist, with an all-equality WHERE, now saves with expected_result_status='captured', expected_rows_affected=1, and a non-null auto_seed.
The same question with WHERE salary > 50000 still fails, and capture_error names the '>' operator rather than the old generic sentence.
A question whose model answer already affects rows captures byte-identically to before and stores auto_seed = NULL — derivation is never called.
A seed whose INSERT violates a foreign key fails at save time with the Postgres error in capture_error, not at grade time.
Reading a saved question back returns the stored auto_seed unchanged; both practice and exam paths behave identically.
After a successful capture, the target table in the real category schema has the same row count as before the save — the seeded row was rolled back.
go build ./... passes; existing capture tests still pass.

arch_decisions.req: Replay the stored seed on the grading and preview paths, inside the existing savepoint, after SET LOCAL ROLE, before the student's statement.
arch_decisions.decision:
Depends on ARCH-038 and ARCH-040b. Edit backend/internal/repository/postgres_evaluation.go ONLY. Two insertion points:
  (1) evaluateDML (:203-230): after SAVEPOINT student_eval, after SET LOCAL search_path and after `SET LOCAL ROLE exam_student`, and BEFORE execStudentStatement.
  (2) evaluateDMLPreview (:442-465): after SAVEPOINT student_eval, after SET LOCAL ROLE <role> and SET LOCAL search_path, and BEFORE execStudentStatement.
At each point: plan, err := unmarshalAutoSeed(question.AutoSeed); if plan is nil, do nothing at all (the overwhelmingly common case must add zero statements). Otherwise call applyAutoSeed.

PLACEMENT AFTER SET LOCAL ROLE IS LOAD-BEARING AND MUST NOT BE 'SIMPLIFIED': the student login roles are created NOINHERIT (postgres_student_pool.go:133), so before SET LOCAL ROLE the connection holds no privileges whatsoever and the INSERT fails. The sandbox roles do hold INSERT on category schemas (postgres_schema.go:179) and exam_student_preview holds full DML on decoy schemas (postgres_preview_schema.go:150). Add a comment saying exactly this so no future reader hoists it.

A failed seed leaves the transaction aborted exactly like a failed student statement: recover with the SAME ordering the file already enforces — ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT student_eval BEFORE RESET ROLE (ARCH-021/ARCH-024b) — and return models.ValidationResult{Status:"error"} (or the PreviewResult equivalent) whose Feedback states the QUESTION is misconfigured and must be re-saved by the lecturer, never wording that blames the submission. That feedback must name no schema, table, role or SQLSTATE, so it survives the ARCH-018 dual-schema scrub. Do not return a Go error for a seed failure on the grading path — that would surface as an HTTP 500.

Applying the seed on BOTH paths is mandatory, not an optimisation: if grading skipped it, a student's correct DELETE would affect 0 rows and be graded wrong; if preview skipped it, the student would see an empty result for a correct statement. Every existing ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT / RESET ROLE ordering in the file must be left exactly as it is.
arch_decisions.rationale: Running inside the already-taken savepoint is the entire reason the real schema is never modified — the seed is discarded by the same ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT that already discards the student's writes. Reading the stored plan instead of re-deriving keeps grading deterministic and costs one JSON unmarshal for questions that have no plan.
acceptance: An auto-seeded DELETE question submitted correctly by a student is graded CORRECT; the same question answered with a no-op statement is graded INCORRECT.
The student's preview of an auto-seeded question shows the seeded row present before their statement and absent after a correct DELETE.
After any number of grades and previews, the target table in the real category schema is byte-identical to before — the seeded row is never committed.
A question with auto_seed NULL executes exactly the statements it does today: no extra round-trip is issued.
A seed that fails at grade time returns Status=error with feedback naming no schema, table, role or SQLSTATE, and does NOT return a Go error / HTTP 500.
ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT still precedes RESET ROLE on every exit path in the file, including the new seed-failure path.
go build ./... passes; existing evaluation and restricted-pool tests still pass.

merge.summary: 8 files reviewed (6 modified backend + 2 new backend + 5 frontend already committed in ea3d5aa); one non-blocking duplicate-helper issue found, everything else clean.

conflicts.issue: Both capture-path implementors independently discovered that models.Question/PracticeQuestion.Type is only ever "QUERY" or "DML" and each added its own package-level helper to detect a leading-INSERT model answer from correct_sql text: isAutoSeedIneligibleInsert() in postgres_practice.go (TODO-005) and isAutoSeedInsertStatement() in postgres_questions.go (TODO-006). Both are byte-for-byte the same logic (strings.TrimSpace(stripSQLComments(sql)) then matchKeywordAt(_, 0, "INSERT")), both reach into dml_autoseed.go's unexported stripSQLComments/matchKeywordAt from the same package, and neither has a naming or compile collision (different names, both build and vet clean, all tests pass). This is not a build-breaking collision or a task-router grouping error -- the two files are correctly file-disjoint and the two TODOs were correctly allowed to run in different parallel waves. It is a design-coordination gap: ARCH-038 froze dml_autoseed.go's public/package API up front but did not anticipate that two downstream capture sites would both need an 'is this an INSERT statement' predicate, so each implementor invented its own copy rather than a shared one. Left as-is, a future change to the INSERT-detection rule (e.g. to also refuse a leading WITH/CTE) has to be made in two places and will silently drift if only one is updated.
conflicts.severity: low - cosmetic duplication only, both implementations verified behaviourally identical, no build/runtime failure
conflicts.recommendation: Route to architect as a small ARCH-038 addendum (promote one helper, e.g. isAutoSeedInsertStatement, to an exported or package-level function *in* dml_autoseed.go, delete the other, and have both capture sites call the single copy) rather than re-running claude-implementor on TODO-005/006 from scratch.
